items.place: Admire the plants at the Wild Gardens of Acadia.
items.snippet: The Wild Gardens of Acadia is home to over 400 native plant species, reflecting the habitats found on Mount Desert Island. Originally founded in 1909, the gardens are open seasonally every morning until dusk, and there is no additional fee to visit.

Acadia has more than 45 miles of rustic carriage roads, a gift from John D. Rockefeller Jr. These car-free crushed gravel roads are the perfect way to explore via bicycle, on foot, or even by horse-drawn carriage. Visitors can rent e-bikes from several local operators, including

Visitors looking to take a swim can opt for saltwater beaches, like Sand Beach, or take a dip in the freshwater Echo Lake. For people looking to take to the sea, the Bar Harbor Whale Watch Co. offers whale-watching expeditions, lighthouse and puffin tours, and island tours.

The Jordan Pond House is the only full-service restaurant inside Acadia National Park, serving its world-famous popovers for more than 100 years. Lunch reservations can be made a month in advance and are recommended, as this is an extremely popular destination for visitors.
